content:
maria_g: escalation from ACME — prod customers are seeing `NXDOMAIN` for our service endpoint `acme-api.svc.prod.internal` after yesterday's tenant VPC peering migration. They report TLS errors too (cert SAN mismatch). Customer says it was working before the migration.

alex_r: :eyes: can you paste the `dig` + `openssl` snippets they sent?

maria_g: pasted from the customer (redacted IPs):
```
$ dig @10.0.2.2 acme-api.svc.prod.internal +short

;; -> (no answer, NXDOMAIN)
```
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.12:443 -servername acme-api.svc.prod.internal
... certificate: CN = api.acme.com, SAN = api.acme.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```
They also say curl returns `curl: (60) SSL certificate: public cert does not match internal name` and their app fails TLS handshake.

sam_k: ok two obvious things to check: 1) private hosted zone association (split-horizon) — confirm the Route53 private hosted zone for `svc.prod.internal` is associated to the customer-prod VPC after the migration; 2) resolver / outbound endpoint egress — their VPC resolver may be hitting an egress ACL that rewrites or forwards to public DNS.

alex_r: to repro on our side, request: `dig @<vpc-resolver-ip> acme-api.svc.prod.internal +trace` from a host in the prod VPC and `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "svc.prod.internal"` then `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z123...` to check VPC associations. Also capture the private endpoint ENI IPs (PrivateLink) — if the private hosted zone isn't associated, PrivateLink will resolve to public and they might get the public cert.

maria_g: customer sent a screenshot of Route53 console — zone exists but associated VPC shown is `customer-dev` not `customer-prod`. They claim we ran a migration script that should have re-associated zones to prod.

sam_k: that explains NXDOMAIN -> if prod VPC doesn't have the private zone associated, the resolver will fall back to public and could return nothing or a different record. The TLS mismatch indicates traffic is reaching the public-facing API (api.acme.com) IP, not the private endpoint.

alex_r: immediate mitigations: 1) re-associate the private hosted zone with the prod VPC (aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone). 2) confirm there are no conflicting resolver rules (outbound endpoints or rule associations) that forward `svc.prod.internal` to an external forwarder. 3) ensure the endpoint security groups allow resolver traffic (UDP/TCP 53) and that NACLs don't drop it.

maria_g: customer asked if egress allowlist could block it — they run a strict egress whitelist. What IPs to allow for Route53 resolver?

sam_k: AWS resolver uses VPC ENIs; there isn't a static public IP list you can allow. If they have a proxy/egress appliance, ensure it permits DNS to the VPC resolver IPs and to the private endpoint ENIs. If they're using a central outbound proxy, add the resolver ENI IPs and the PrivateLink ENI IPs (the VPC endpoint ENIs) to the allowlist. Also check firewall logs for dropped connections to port 53 and 443 to those ENIs.

alex_r: added a checklist for triage (assigning to @sam_k):
- confirm which VPCs are associated with the `svc.prod.internal` private hosted zone (route53 console + CLI)
- run `dig @<resolver-ip> acme-api.svc.prod.internal +short` from a prod host (capture full packet if possible)
- verify private endpoint (PrivateLink) ENI IPs and that TLS server cert on the private endpoint matches `acme-api.svc.prod.internal`
- check egress/proxy/firewall logs for blocked DNS/TCP 443 to resolver/enis
- if zone not associated, re-associate and confirm TTL/propagation (usually immediate for private zones)

maria_g: customer gave permission to share console access logs. I've uploaded the S3 bundle link in the ticket.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-3145 assigned to `sam_k`. Priority: high.

sam_k: I'll re-associate the hosted zone to prod and validate. If re-association isn't allowed (cross-account), we may need the customer to run the `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` in their account or whitelabel assuming role.

alex_r: after re-assoc, run `dig` again and `openssl s_client -connect <private-ip>:443 -servername acme-api.svc.prod.internal` to confirm cert SAN matches. Also check our side that the private endpoint is serving the internal cert (we package internal certs onto PrivateLink services).

maria_g: I'll coordinate with the customer on access. Customer impact: majority of prod traffic for one tenant failing (timeout + TLS).

sam_k: action plan: 1) attempt re-assoc (if we have cross-account perms), 2) if not possible, send precise CLI/console steps to customer and stay on zoom while they run it, 3) confirm egress allowlist includes resolver ENI IPs and PrivateLink ENIs. I'll post updates here.

maria_g: thanks — I'll keep ticket updated and add the zoom link. Please ping me when complete so I can notify customer. :thumbsup:

alex_r: one more note — check for any node-local caches (dnsmasq / CoreDNS stubDomains) on their hosts that may be caching the NXDOMAIN; if present clear caches after re-assoc.

maria_g: got it. current ETA for first action (re-assoc) — 20m. will update.

sam_k: starting now.

(END OF THREAD)
